results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: [Optional (if the ref might be invalid/ambiguous)] [Prerequisite]: Resolve/validate the target revision using GITHUB_GET_A_COMMIT (avoid querying checks for a missing or foreign ref).

[Required] [Step]: Enumerate check runs for the revision using GITHUB_LIST_CHECK_RUNS_FOR_A_REF (read response.data.total_count and response.data.check_runs; capture id, name, status, conclusion, and web URL fields; if any status is not "completed", re-call until stable; if total_count=0 with no error, treat as “no reported check runs”).
[Optional (if a run is failing/in_progress or you need full output)] [Next Step]: Fetch the selected run using GITHUB_GET_CHECK_RUN (inspect output title/summary/text and linked metadata).
[Optional (if annotations_count > 0 and you need file/line context)] [Next Step]: Retrieve annotations using GITHUB_LIST_CHECK_RUN_ANNOTATIONS (review path/line/message when available).

[Optional (if check run details/annotations are insufficient for troubleshooting)] [Fallback]: Trace related CI execution via GITHUB_LIST_WORKFLOW_RUNS_FOR_A_REPOSITORY → GITHUB_LIST_JOBS_FOR_A_WORKFLOW_RUN → GITHUB_DOWNLOAD_JOB_LOGS_FOR_A_WORKFLOW_RUN (map errors back to failing job/step).
known_pitfalls: [GITHUB_LIST_CHECK_RUNS_FOR_A_REF] HTTP 422 when the ref/SHA is not present in the repository context; payloads can be very large and may be truncated—extract only key fields.
[GITHUB_GET_A_COMMIT] HTTP 422 when the commit SHA is invalid for the repository.
[GITHUB_LIST_CHECK_RUNS_FOR_A_REF] response.data.check_runs may be empty (total_count can be 0) even for a valid ref; interpret as “no reported checks” unless an error is returned.
[GITHUB_LIST_CHECK_RUNS_FOR_A_REF] In-progress runs may have conclusion null/None; rely on status to distinguish running vs completed.
[GITHUB_DOWNLOAD_JOB_LOGS_FOR_A_WORKFLOW_RUN] Requires job_id (not check_run_id); downloaded logs may include escaped newlines ("\\n") requiring splitting before scanning error lines.

reference_workbench_snippets.description: Extract key fields from a GITHUB_LIST_CHECK_RUNS_FOR_A_REF response object
Parse downloaded job log payloads that may contain escaped newlines ("\\n") and extract nearby failure lines
reference_workbench_snippets.code:
```python
log_text=str(job_logs)
lines=log_text.split('\\n')
keys=['##[error]','exit code','failed','error']
out=[]
for i,l in enumerate(lines):
    if any(k in l.lower() for k in keys):
        out=lines[max(0,i-3):i+10];break
'\n'.join(out[:80])
```

GITHUB_GET_A_COMMIT.description: Retrieves a specific commit from a repository by its owner, name, and a valid commit reference (SHA, branch, or tag), supporting pagination for large diffs.

ref.description: The commit reference. Can be a commit SHA (e.g., '`sha`'), a branch name (e.g., 'heads/`BRANCH_NAME`' or simply '`BRANCH_NAME`'), or a tag name (e.g., 'tags/`TAG_NAME`'). For more information, see "[Git References](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Internals-Git-References)" in the Git documentation.

owner.description: The username or organization name that owns the repository. This field is not case-sensitive.

GITHUB_LIST_WORKFLOW_RUNS_FOR_A_REPOSITO.description: Lists workflow runs for a repository, allowing filtering by actor, branch, event, status, creation date, check suite ID, or head SHA; the repository must exist and be accessible.

page.description: Page number of the results to fetch.

actor.description: Filter by the actor's login (e.g., the user who triggered the `push`).

event.description: Filter by the event that triggered the workflow (e.g., `push`, `pull_request`).

owner.description: The account owner of the repository (not case-sensitive).

branch.description: Filter by branch name (e.g., `main` or the branch that triggered the `push`).

status.description: Filter by `status` or `conclusion` (e.g., `success`, `in_progress`). Note: Only GitHub Actions can set `waiting`, `pending`, or `requested`.

created.description: Filter by creation date or date-time range (ISO8601 format: YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ). Supports operators like `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`, and `..` for ranges.

head_sha.description: Filter to include only runs associated with the specified `head_sha` (commit SHA at the head of the branch).

exclude_pull_requests.description: Set to `true` to exclude workflow runs triggered by pull request events. Omit or leave as null to include all runs.
